title: How an Octopus Changes Color
note: The complete explanation accurately separates visible skin change from the unresolved question of how octopuses process visual information. Chromatophores, their pigment sacs, muscular control and additional reflective skin structures agree with the Smithsonian account; the cautious final paragraph avoids claiming human-like color vision.

title: A City Without Cars
note: The original announces a fictional policy scenario but classifies it as nonfiction, then presents invented sales reports and a “real information” conclusion as if an actual trial had been measured. Recast it as an explicitly imagined city decision; keep the business, delivery and accessibility tradeoffs, and avoid claiming a single month proves an outcome.

title: Last Seat on the Train

title: Girl Who Delivered Letters
note: Although labeled fictional, the original asserts that historians found records of a secretly employed woman rider and a later discovered letter. No source accompanies those claims. Make the rider, company, towns and letter expressly invented and remove the purported documentary discovery, while preserving a coherent historical-style narrative and the economic motive.

title: Why Bread Rises
note: The original correctly identifies yeast fermentation and gas retention, but describes yeast as eating sugar “in the flour,” treats oven rise as gas expansion alone, and says the outside simply hardens to lock the shape. Revise it to distinguish available sugars, proofing, gas and steam expansion, and the setting of starch and proteins during baking.

title: Cartographer's Mistake
note: The fictional mirage has a coherent series of independent sightings, investigation and tentative explanation, but the final instruction to trust a compass rather than one’s eyes wrongly implies a compass alone determines whether land exists. Clarify that observations and bearings must be checked across journeys; the optical explanation remains a possibility rather than a proven diagnosis.

title: How Birds Can Change Their Migration Routes
note: The full passage presents migration as a flexible behavior shaped by inherited orientation, experience, weather, food, social learning and changing conditions rather than as a fixed map. Cornell Lab material supports independent juvenile migration, multiple navigation cues, individual weather-related variation, artificial-light hazards and modern tracking methods; the text appropriately warns against generalizing from one journey.

title: The Fishing Village That Said No
note: The original fictional scenario is classified as nonfiction and ends with invented economists studying a documented case; it also implies that rejecting a processing plant by itself prevents fish depletion. Recast the village and vote as expressly imagined, distinguish processing capacity from fishing limits, and include monitoring and the economic costs of the choice.

title: Learning to Cook From Scratch
note: The original narrative is coherent but describes a fixed rice-to-water ratio and adding oil only after a pan is properly hot as universal cooking rules; these vary by rice, method and pan. Replace the broad rules with concrete recipe-following and observation, retain Priya’s gradual learning, and connect the final reflection to the dinner she actually makes.

title: Bridge Built in a Single Winter
note: The opening says the bridge is invented, yet the ending claims local historians still cite it. The ice-supported construction and six-year survival also imply an implausibly certain engineering outcome. Write a self-contained fictional winter footbridge with bank-supported work, an inspection and removal before thaw, preserving the workers’ need for a safer crossing without presenting a fabricated historical case.

title: What the Brain Does During Sleep
note: The complete explanation accurately describes sleep stages, memory support, attention and emotional effects while preserving uncertainty around brain-fluid clearance. The glymphatic paragraph correctly identifies the strongest direct clearance experiment as animal research and does not present the mechanism as a settled human “brain wash.”

title: Clockmaker's Apprentice
note: The original contains a sentence fragment (“However, in a pattern”), leaves the gear’s star pattern unexplained and ends without resolving the client’s deadline. Rebuild the clue as a deliberately engraved sky chart that helps locate a missing spring, show Teodor testing the repair and give the client a concrete reason for returning.

title: Leafcutter Ants and Their Fungus Garden
note: The complete account correctly distinguishes the leaves used as a fungal substrate from the cultivated fungus eaten by ants, describes a queen carrying starter fungus, and limits the bacteria defense to some leafcutter relatives. The medical-use sentence remains explicitly speculative. The original leafcutter-genome study and studies of Acromyrmex defensive symbionts support the main claims; no change to the full text is needed.

title: When a River Crosses a Border
note: The original overstates an absence of binding international frameworks, treats adverse dam effects as inevitable, and claims compensation is typical of successful agreements. The 1997 UN Watercourses Convention sets equitable and reasonable use, prevention of significant harm, exchange of information and notification of planned measures for its parties, while river-specific agreements vary. Replace sweeping claims with a hypothetical case and accurately bounded treaty description.

title: Apartment Above the Bakery
note: The narrative’s basic arc is clear, but most sentences are overloaded with qualifications and the almost imperceptible kneading sounds are an odd source of lost sleep. Make the early-morning disturbance concrete, give Marcus and the baker a conversation about noise, and let the ending grow from a workable arrangement rather than passive acceptance alone.

title: Telegraph Operator Who Changed a War
note: The opening labels the account fictional but invents official military records, later historians and current citations, falsely implying a documented case. Remove those claims, make the war and operator openly invented, and avoid presenting a two-hour delay as certainly preventing friendly fire. Preserve the dilemma, request for clarification, and a limited outcome witnessed by the character.

title: Spirals in Seashell Growth
note: The full explanation accurately describes accretion at the shell edge, the use of an approximate logarithmic or equiangular spiral for many coiled shells, limits of a mathematical model, and the lack of a common physical mechanism behind superficially similar galactic and biological spirals. University of Tokyo museum material confirms the growth and model distinction; no change is needed. NASA and NOAA also support the distinction between galactic density-wave patterns and storm circulation.

title: Archivist's Debt
note: The original spends its length setting up the cipher and locked room, then withholds what Ilsabet discovers, so neither the debt nor her changed behavior is intelligible. Give the old promise a concrete object, let the key date follow from the deciphered record, and show her decision to make suppressed testimony accessible.

title: Life Around Deep-Sea Hydrothermal Vents
note: The full passage coherently traces the 1977 Pacific discovery, seawater circulation, chemosynthesis, adult tube-worm symbiosis and a carefully limited astrobiology implication. NOAA, WHOI and NASA confirm the factual claims, including blood-borne chemicals to the symbionts. Level 8 terminology is explained in sequence; the text does not imply that deep-sea animals were wholly unknown or that alien life has been found.

title: Who Keeps the Digital Currency Record?
note: The original falsely implies that governments or banks issued almost all money throughout history, treats all distributed assets as beyond concentrated influence, and overstates inflation protection and inclusion. Its sentences are unusually dense and its migration subtopic unrelated. Rewrite as a bounded explanation of permissionless ledgers, distinguish them from other digital money, qualify benefits and risks, and identify the electricity issue specifically with mining. BIS and IMF institutional analyses support the revised claims.

title: Neighbor Who Kept Score
note: The original finds an empathetic motive for Hendricks’s notes but leaves Renata’s anxiety and the intrusive behavior largely unchanged. Retain the outage and bereavement while having the neighbors agree on a shared channel for genuine building concerns and a limit on personal notes.

title: Committee That Erased Itself
note: The piece calls itself fictional yet states that government historians later studied a particular commission, presenting a fabricated event as recorded history. Its authority problem also needs a concrete procedure. Frame the account as an invented government, pause the destruction of records, obtain legal advice and show the council closing the group while preserving its report.

title: Baker Who Whispered to Bread
note: The story suggests an old starter sits bubbling in dozens of pots and that every loaf literally contains part of every previous loaf. Recast the starter as a single culture Oskar feeds and uses regularly, while keeping the dialogue and lesson that a whispered phrase cannot replace technique and patient fermentation.

title: Door That Only Opened at Noon
note: The original has Nessa arrive after school just before noon, an impossible sequence for an ordinary school day, and places her return at the last strike of the same twelve-bell chime after she spends a minute in the meadow. Move the visit to a free Saturday and use a short open interval with a visible closing cue.

title: The Tailor's Invisible Thread
note: The complete Level 6 fantasy is internally consistent: the visible tear, the tailor’s inherited invisible thread, the widower’s wish to preserve the dress, and the later decision to lock the spool away follow in order. It makes no claim that such thread exists outside the fictional village; the prose and pronouns need no change.

title: River That Remembered Names
note: The river’s voice is a clear fantasy premise, but Tomasz strikes his head, nearly drowns and resumes fishing with no response to the injury, while the repeated superstition debate adds little. Give a companion a concrete rescue role, make him rest and seek help for the head injury, and let his later respect for the river lead to safer fishing.

title: Clockmaker's Second Apprentice
note: The apprentice’s gift predicts failures without any particular test, consequence or recognition, and the master quietly takes credit. Make one prediction concrete, have Halvard check a clock for a developing fault, and give Ren explicit shared credit while leaving the fantasy gift unexplained.

title: The Garden Grown From Borrowed Time
note: The original sets up a magical cost to each flower but ends by avoiding Ingrid’s decision, leaving no action or consequence. Show her choosing ordinary growth for part of the garden, tell a neighbor enough to make the choice visible, and retain some uncertainty about the bargain’s exact cost rather than asserting an unmeasured exchange.

title: Cartographer Who Sold Directions
note: The premise promises personalized directions to impossible places but reports outcomes only as vague revelations and a silent widower, so the reader cannot evaluate the service or its cost. Give the widower a specific route to a present-day location connected to his memory, let him state what it did and did not restore, and preserve the cartographer’s limits.

title: Innkeeper's Ledger of Debts
note: Corvin’s invisible moral debts are a fantasy device, but the original has him secretly create inconveniences and judge guests without consent, with no witnessed resolution. Have him offer a conversation and a practical chance to repair a broken promise, leaving the guest free to decide.

title: How Crows Learn a Dangerous Face
note: The original is generally based on a real field study but dramatizes immediate recognition, calls all masks rubber without need, and leaps from five years of observations to a claim that the information outlives any individual crow. The original study distinguished crows captured by masked researchers, uncaptured adults learning in groups, and young birds learning from parents. Rewrite the account with measured observations and the study's limits; correct the unrelated plants-and-fungi subtopic. Short clauses, chronological sequencing and clear referents suit Level 5.
